**Compensation: $110,000\-$150,000 annually\***


Dudek’s journey began in 1980 with a vision to serve Southern California’s water and wastewater agencies.


Today, we are a 100% employee\-owned firm supporting clients nationwide and delivering projects that improve and protect the built and natural environments of communities throughout the United States. Our work has been recognized by leading industry organizations, and we’ve been honored with multiple national Top Workplace Awards.


Our employee\-owners are unified by a singular commitment to supporting projects that address key societal issues, such as the transition to renewable energy, infrastructure hardening and repair, environmental protection, and community resilience.


Learn more about our **award\-winning culture**, the **benefits and perks** of being a Dudekian, and the **projects** you will have the opportunity to shape.


Position Overview:
**Who You Are**


As an **employee\-owner**, you embrace accountability, working safely, and collaboration while thinking resourcefully and independently.


Like all Dudekians, you are curious and **solution\-oriented**, with the ability to adapt quickly to changes and approach challenges with a spirit of **innovation**.

**How** **You’ll** **Make an Impact**


We are seeking a senior\-level professional to lead environmental compliance services supporting complex infrastructure and renewable energy projects. This role will serve as a key partner to clients and project teams by guiding compliance strategy, managing environmental commitments, and ensuring successful implementation of permit conditions throughout the project lifecycle.


You will lead compliance efforts for projects including utility\-scale solar, battery energy storage systems (BESS), transmission and linear infrastructure, and other renewable energy developments, coordinating closely with multidisciplinary teams, contractors, and regulatory agencies. This position combines project management, client engagement, and technical leadership to help projects move forward efficiently while maintaining regulatory compliance and environmental stewardship.


This position will primarily be office based. There will be opportunities for field work and travel, but the majority of the work will be completed in Dudek’s office or working from a home office.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

* Promote a culture of teamwork, engagement, quality service, and customer satisfaction to our clients.
* Foster client connections through existing client relationships and proactive business development in the candidate’s areas of strength and interest, working with others to anticipate and pursue work
* Enhance Dudek’s professional reputation and demonstrate the ability to be creative and innovative with these tasks while representing Dudek in a professional manner
* Work closely with other Dudek Project Managers to promote our business interests in adherence with the company’s mission, vision, and values
* Lead the preparation, organization, and production of environmental compliance management plans, permit applications, and other environmental documents to guide compliance implementation during the project lifecycle.
* Work with project team members to track environmental commitments to support the implementation of permit conditions on a variety of projects.
* Coordinate with client, field personnel, and environmental resource specialists to ensure permit conditions are implemented during construction.
* Prepare bid documents and proposals

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, or other related field.
* A minimum of at least 12 years of combined experience leading teams in complex project due\-diligence, large infrastructure project management, preparing permitting and environmental documents, managing, and supervising staff, and overseeing technical quality.
* Must demonstrate strong technical writing and research skills as well as solid written and verbal communication skills.
* Highly organized with the ability to multi\-task in a fast\-paced environment.
* Must be proficient in MS Office, in particular Word and Excel.
* Customarily and regularly exercises discretion and independent judgment.
* Self\-motivated with an interest to learn and grow as a project team.
* Must possess a valid driver’s license and have active personal automobile liability insurance by first day of employment

 **Preferred Qualifications**

* Advanced degree in environmental science, planning, or related field
* Experience working within an environmental consulting firm or AEC consulting environment
* Familiarity with California energy market or utility client programs
* Experience supporting large, multi\-disciplinary project teams across multiple offices or regions
* Demonstrated involvement in internal initiatives such as process improvement, mentoring programs, or practice development
* Existing client relationships within the renewable energy or infrastructure sectors

**Compensation:** $110,000\-$150,000 annually\*

* Final agreed\-upon compensation will be based on a variety of factors including, but not limited to, an individual’s related experience, education, certifications, skills, and work location. Successful candidates must pass a pre\-employment drug test and background check prior to beginning employment.

* This job operates in a remote or office\-based environment and this role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, printers, etc.
* This job requires occasional project site visits, based outdoors which can include excessive noise, uneven walking surfaces, extreme weather, and moving vehicles and equipment.

jobs.title: Superannuation Operations Specialist - Incident & Remediation
jobs.description:
### **Description**

 **About Future Group**
Future Group is not your traditional financial services company – we're a collective of super funds and services committed to changing our planet now for a better tomorrow. When you join us, you’ll become part of a team united by a clear and important mission: to lead the investment movement by advocating and campaigning for a future worth retiring into.  

We are looking for someone to join our purpose\-led high\-growth scale\-up as a Superannuation Operations Specialist – Incident \& Remediation on a six\-month fixed\-term contract.  

  

This role is an opportunity for someone with experience in superannuation administration to take the next step in their career by moving into Trustee services. You’ll support the Trustee’s approach to incidents, breaches and remediation across the Fund and its service providers. You’ll work with senior Fund Operations colleagues and internal and external stakeholders to assess incidents, understand their impact, support remediation activities and help strengthen processes and controls.  

You may already be working in a superannuation Trustee office, or you may be joining us from a superannuation administrator and looking to broaden your experience into governance, oversight and Trustee responsibilities. And the best bit, you’ll get to work with some fantastic work mates!  

Future Group values diverse lived experience and identities, and we strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander backgrounds, those with caring responsibilities, from culturally and racially marginalised groups, with disabilities, who experience ageism, LGBTQIA\+ individuals, and those who face social exclusion due to their social class.  

  

We recognise that the recruitment journey may present unique challenges for trans and gender diverse folk, and we are committed to ensuring an inclusive and accessible recruitment process for all. We will happily make any reasonable adjustments to accommodate diverse needs, so if there is anything we can do to support you at any stage of your application, please let us know. For more information about DEIB at Future Group, please contact us at diversity@futuregroup.com.au.  

  

**About The Role**  

As our Superannuation Operations Specialist – Incident \& Remediation, you’ll support the identification, assessment and management of incidents, breaches and remediation activities.  

You’ll help gather information, review incident assessments, analyse root causes and support the assessment of impacts on members, the Fund and financial outcomes. You’ll also assist with reviewing remediation proposals, tracking agreed actions and ensuring matters are documented and followed through appropriately.  

Working with internal teams and service providers, you’ll help identify recurring issues, emerging risks and opportunities to improve controls and processes. You’ll contribute to incident reporting, governance activities and the delivery of fair, timely and well\-documented remediation outcomes for members.### **You'll love this job if**

  

* You enjoy investigating problems and working out what happened, why it happened and what needs to happen next.
* You have a strong eye for detail and are comfortable working with data, evidence and financial information.
* You like asking thoughtful questions and constructively challenging information when required.
* You’re organised and able to manage several matters and deadlines at the same time.
* You enjoy working with a range of stakeholders to resolve issues and improve outcomes.
* You like working in a changing environment where you can contribute ideas and learn new areas of superannuation operations.

  

### **We're looking for someone who**

  

* Has experience in superannuation, particularly understanding Trustee obligations, with exposure to incidents, errors, breaches, remediation or operational risk.
* Understands how errors or process failures can affect members, financial outcomes and Trustee obligations.
* Has experience investigating issues, gathering information, identifying root causes and tracking corrective actions.
* Ideally has experience working in a superannuation Trustee office, or has worked closely with a Trustee, RSE licensee or service\-provider oversight function.
* Has strong analytical, organisational, written and verbal communication skills.
* Can interpret information, identify inconsistencies and maintain clear and accurate records.
* Is comfortable working with administrators, insurers, service providers and internal stakeholders.
* Has RG146 or is willing to undertake the relevant training where required for the role.
* Believes in Future Group’s mission and has a passion for moving Australia’s money out of fossil fuels and into renewable energy.
* Believes in using the power of money to build a sustainable and equitable world.

**Some nice\-to\-haves but are not essential are:*** Experience supporting incident, breach or remediation assessments.
* Exposure to superannuation legislation, APRA or ASIC requirements.
* Experience with risk registers, governance reporting, root cause analysis or control improvement.

  

### **Why would you enjoy working at Future Group?**

  

* A purpose\-driven organisation \- spend your days working on making this world a better place! The more we grow, the bigger the impact we are making on climate change and inequality
* A B Corp organisation that cares about how it behaves inside and out
* AFR's Best Place to Work 2026! Proud winners of TWO awards: Best Medium Organisation, and our industry category of Banking, Superannuation and Financial Services (an award we also won in 2022!)
* Flexibility to fit work into your life (not your life around our work). School drop\-offs/pick\-ups and lunch\-time gym sessions are a thing here
* The choice to work from home, from one of our co\-working spaces, from anywhere within Australia or even from overse

jobs.title: Creative Director, Brand
jobs.description:
Nex is on a mission to help families rediscover the joy of movement. Created by parents for parents, Nex combines technology and play to deliver fun, social, and interactive experiences powered by natural body motion, encouraging kids and adults to move more, play more, and have fun together. Nex Playground, the company's award\-winning active play system, is purpose\-built to get families moving year\-round, with safety and privacy as core considerations in its intentional design. It is certified kidSAFE\+ COPPA compliant and built to support healthy, active play for all ages and abilities.



Nex Playground features a growing library of 50\+ experiences, including motion and dance games, fitness and educational experiences, and Nex Originals. Content includes collaborations with partners like Hasbro, Sesame Workshop, and NBCUniversal. Nex has been recognized by Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, TIME's Best Inventions, and Parents' Best Entertainment System for Families, and has earned Red Dot, IDEA, and Core77 international design awards. We encourage you to explore Have Fun and Is Motion Gaming Back?, as they offer a deeper look into our culture, values, and explain how our approach to motion gaming differs from previous generations.



To protect yourself from recruitment scams, please note that Nex communicates through official company emails ending in @nex.inc. If you receive a suspicious email or message, please do not respond and report it immediately to us.

**Location:** Remote (US \& Canada only)  

**Annual salary:** $180,000 \- $210,000 USD (Final base salary within this range will be determined based on job\-related factors, including the candidate's experience, skills, qualifications, and geographic location)  

**Type:** Full Time  

**Reports to:** VP of Design



Nex has always been design\-led. There's deep ex\-Apple DNA on the team, and we make decisions from first principles rather than by copying whatever our competitors shipped last quarter. We're looking for a Creative Director to raise the creative quality of everything Nex puts into the world. This is rare opportunity to help mold the creative organization's culture and scale it up as the team grows. You'll lead and develop our marketing creative team while remaining deeply involved in the work itself. You'll help shape campaign concepts, establish creative direction, develop ideas, review work, and occasionally get your hands dirty when the work needs it. But your greatest impact will come from making the people and work around you better. You'll take broad marketing and business objectives and turn them into creative work that people actually want to see.



We're not looking for someone who simply knows how to make polished advertising. We're looking for someone who knows how to make great ideas. Someone who can recognize a genuinely original idea when they see it, push a good idea into a great one, and know when something isn't good enough to ship. You should have a track record of creating campaigns that people remember, talk about, and share.


**What you'll do**
------------------


### **Lead the creative**


* Own creative direction for Nex's marketing campaigns and communications, from concept through launch.
* + Translate business objectives into compelling creative strategies and ideas.
	+ Develop and challenge concepts, platforms, and campaign directions.
	+ Push the team toward work that is distinctive, surprising, and memorable.
	+ Set the creative vision and maintain it through execution.
	+ Set and uphold a high creative bar across campaigns, paid media, social, retail, launches, and partnerships.
	+ Know when work is good, great, or not ready to ship, and have the authority to redirect it when needed.

### **Make the work**


* Stay close to the craft while empowering the team to execute.
* + Concept and pitch ideas; develop creative directions, mood boards, style frames, and visual approaches.
	+ Art direct creative production across design, motion, illustration, photography, and other mediums.
	+ Get hands\-on in creative tools when useful.
	+ Give clear, actionable feedback that materially improves the work.
	+ Know when to step in and when to let the team own the execution.
	+ Your job is to make sure the right idea gets made exceptionally well.

### **Build a great creative team**


* Lead and develop our marketing creative team and future creative talent.
* + Coach creatives to strengthen craft, conceptual thinking, strategic judgment, and presentation skills.
	+ Build a culture of candid critique, experimentation, high standards, and low ego.
	+ Create an environment where people actively seek feedback and grow from it.
	+ Hire thoughtfully and raise the caliber of the team as Nex grows.

### **Make creative reviews better**


* Great creative teams don't need more meetings \- they need better ones.
* + Establish focused, efficient creative reviews with clear decision\-making.
	+ Help distinguish strategic feedback, creative feedback, and personal preference.
	+ Build processes and rituals that enable speed without compromising quality.
	+ Continuously improve how the team briefs, develops, reviews, and ships creative.

### **Be a strategic partner**


* Collaborate with partners to turn business objectives into creative opportunities.
* + Challenge briefs and bring creative thinking into strategy early.
	+ Identify opportunities to make Nex more culturally relevant and distinctive.
	+ Present and defend creative thinking with confidence and clarity.
	+ Balance creative ambition with audience needs, business goals, timelines, and resources.

### **Build trust across Nex**


* Build strong relationships with senior partners.

	+ Bring people along without letting consensus replace good creative judgment.
	+ Be a thoughtful advocate for the work while staying pragmatic.

Nex Playground features a growing library of 50\+ experiences, including motion and dance games, fitness and educational experiences, and Nex Originals. Content includes collaborations with partners like Hasbro, Sesame Workshop, and NBCUniversal. Nex has been recognized by Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, TIME's Best Inventions, and Parents' Best Entertainment System for Families, and has earned Red Dot, IDEA, and Core77 international design awards. We encourage you to explore Have Fun and Is Motion Gaming Back?, as they offer a deeper look into our culture, values, and explain how our approach to motion gaming differs from previous generations.



To protect yourself from recruitment scams, please note that Nex communicates through official company emails ending in @nex.inc. If you receive a suspicious email or message, please do not respond and report it immediately to us.

**Location:** Remote (US \& Canada only)  

**Annual salary:** $180,000 \- $210,000 USD (Final base salary within this range will be determined based on job\-related factors, including the candidate's experience, skills, qualifications, and geographic location)  

**Type:** 6 month contract with potential FTE conversion  

**Reports to:** VP of Design



Nex has always been design\-led. There's deep ex\-Apple DNA on the team, and we make decisions from first principles rather than by copying whatever our competitors shipped last quarter. We're looking for a Creative Director to raise the creative quality of everything Nex puts into the world. This is rare opportunity to help mold the creative organization's culture and scale it up as the team grows. You'll lead and develop our marketing creative team while remaining deeply involved in the work itself. You'll help shape campaign concepts, establish creative direction, develop ideas, review work, and occasionally get your hands dirty when the work needs it. But your greatest impact will come from making the people and work around you better. You'll take broad marketing and business objectives and turn them into creative work that people actually want to see.



We're not looking for someone who simply knows how to make polished advertising. We're looking for someone who knows how to make great ideas. Someone who can recognize a genuinely original idea when they see it, push a good idea into a great one, and know when something isn't good enough to ship. You should have a track record of creating campaigns that people remember, talk about, and share.


**What you'll do**
------------------


### **Lead the creative**


* Own creative direction for Nex's marketing campaigns and communications, from concept through launch.
* + Translate business objectives into compelling creative strategies and ideas.
	+ Develop and challenge concepts, platforms, and campaign directions.
	+ Push the team toward work that is distinctive, surprising, and memorable.
	+ Set the creative vision and maintain it through execution.
	+ Set and uphold a high creative bar across campaigns, paid media, social, retail, launches, and partnerships.
	+ Know when work is good, great, or not ready to ship, and have the authority to redirect it when needed.

### **Make the work**


* Stay close to the craft while empowering the team to execute.
* + Concept and pitch ideas; develop creative directions, mood boards, style frames, and visual approaches.
	+ Art direct creative production across design, motion, illustration, photography, and other mediums.
	+ Get hands\-on in creative tools when useful.
	+ Give clear, actionable feedback that materially improves the work.
	+ Know when to step in and when to let the team own the execution.
	+ Your job is to make sure the right idea gets made exceptionally well.

### **Build a great creative team**


* Lead and develop our marketing creative team and future creative talent.
* + Coach creatives to strengthen craft, conceptual thinking, strategic judgment, and presentation skills.
	+ Build a culture of candid critique, experimentation, high standards, and low ego.
	+ Create an environment where people actively seek feedback and grow from it.
	+ Hire thoughtfully and raise the caliber of the team as Nex grows.

### **Make creative reviews better**


* Great creative teams don't need more meetings \- they need better ones.
* + Establish focused, efficient creative reviews with clear decision\-making.
	+ Help distinguish strategic feedback, creative feedback, and personal preference.
	+ Build processes and rituals that enable speed without compromising quality.
	+ Continuously improve how the team briefs, develops, reviews, and ships creative.

### **Be a strategic partner**


* Collaborate with partners to turn business objectives into creative opportunities.
* + Challenge briefs and bring creative thinking into strategy early.
	+ Identify opportunities to make Nex more culturally relevant and distinctive.
	+ Present and defend creative thinking with confidence and clarity.
	+ Balance creative ambition with audience needs, business goals, timelines, and resources.

### **Build trust across Nex**


* Build strong relationships with senior partners.
* + Help non\-creative stakeholders understand what makes creative effective.
	+ Bring people along without letting consensus replace good creative judgment.
	+ Be a thoughtful advocate for the work while staying pragmatic.

jobs.title: Portfolio Delivery Leader - Environmental Remediation Sector
jobs.description:
**Company Description** **Work with Us. Change the World.**


At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.


There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.


We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

 **Job Description**  

AECOM is looking to hire a Portfolio Delivery Leaders (PDL) to oversee projects and project teams within our Environmental Remediation Group. The role is set up to be remote, however we will need the candidate to reside within the United States of America.


The PDL will report directly to the Practice Operations Lead, will serve as Project Director, and will be responsible for overseeing a portfolio of projects in the Remediation Practice of the Environment Business Line. The PDL will work closely with the Project Managers responsible for these projects to grow their financial acumen, project management capabilities, and drive overall project performance. The PDL will support the Practice Operations Lead in meeting Business Line objectives in the areas of financial profitability, project delivery, risk management, commercial terms evaluation, and budgeting and forecasting.


The ideal candidate for this opportunity has a natural drive and ability to communicate effectively with all levels of stakeholders, both internally and externally. The ideal PDL must have the ability to present information in a confident and concise manner to stakeholders. This opportunity requires someone who enjoys building relationships, is a team player, operates and responds in a fast\-paced environment with less than complete information, is well\-organized to understand priorities, and is familiar with the challenges projects with a variety of scopes and contract types bring.

**Responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to:**

* Accountability for the planning, safe execution, and delivery of a portfolio of Environment projects at As Sold or better financial KPIs.
* Evaluating day\-to\-day project delivery performance, pricing strategies, risk management, forecasting and budgeting, and performance reporting for a ranging portfolio of Environment clients and projects.
* Interpreting project performance figures to support risk evaluation and financial forecasting.
* Providing proactive and hands\-on support to project managers to support strong financial monitoring, prevent project issues, address risks, and make recommendations to improve project performance. This includes analyzing project costs, billings and schedules, driving cash flow, trouble\-shooting problems both common and unique, supporting mitigation measures, and being “root cause oriented” in the resolution of issues.
* Ensuring appropriate scheduling tools and processes are in use by the project team and are supported by the Project Controller (PC) and/or PDL.
* Providing support to Project Managers (PM) by:
* Fully understanding applicable contracts
* Leading comprehensive project reviews covering scope, schedule, budget, risk, quality, resourcing, and client\-focused agenda topics
* Engaging project team at all milestones
* Proactive management of change (cost, revenue budget, schedule, etc.)
* Supporting dispute resolution, where required
* Supporting timely and accurate Estimate\-at\-Completion (EAC) preparation and review
* Proactively engaging project stakeholders
* Identifying and implementing appropriate tools to track physical % complete and translate to Earned Value Management
* Developing strong deputy project managers.
* In partnership with Project Controls leadership, mentoring and directing the work of Project Controls staff to appropriately support both the common and unique needs of their assigned portfolio.
* Assisting in the development and review of proposal resource plans, schedules and pricing that aligns with business line objectives and individual bid strategies. Supporting the client service/business development staff on key pursuits (e.g., initial evaluation of terms and conditions, commercial risk, and competitive advantage).
* In coordination with the Department or Program Manager, providing guidance in assigning projects and pursuit efforts to project managers.
* In partnership with the Department or Program Manager, continually evaluating performance of project managers within the portfolio, and mentoring project management staff to ensure timely, effective, and efficient performance of responsibilities.
* Fostering career growth of project managers.
* Developing PM risk competencies, including a strong contractual understanding of risk and contingency management
* Supporting project managers and project team members with invoicing and cash collection strategy. Reviewing unbilled/accounts receivable portfolios and making recommendations for improved performance to drive appropriate Days Sales Outstanding (DSO).
* Driving consistent project management practices and procedures in alignment with AECOM PM requirements.
* Evaluating and driving AECOM delivery excellence practices including Healthy Start project reviews.

 **Qualifications** **Minimum Requirements:**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Environmental Sciences or comparable technical or business professional degree AND 4 years of relevant experience or demons

**Location: Irvine, CA \| Hybrid Field \& Office Role**

Make an Impact on Environmental Compliance \& Sustainability

Are you passionate about protecting the environment and helping organizations stay compliant with environmental regulations? We are seeking an Environmental Scientist to join a growing team supporting environmental compliance programs across a variety of industries.

This is an excellent opportunity for an early\-career environmental professional who enjoys a mix of office and field work, values professional growth, and wants exposure to a wide range of environmental regulations and compliance programs. You'll work alongside experienced environmental professionals, interact with clients, and gain hands\-on experience conducting compliance audits, inspections, sampling, and technical reporting.

**Work Schedule:** Approximately 50% office and 50% field work, including travel to client facilities throughout California and other locations as needed.

What You'll Do

* Conduct environmental compliance audits, inspections, and site assessments.
* Support hazardous waste, regulated waste, RCRA, stormwater, air quality, and related environmental compliance programs.
* Collect, analyze, and interpret environmental data.
* Prepare technical reports, regulatory documentation, and compliance deliverables.
* Research environmental regulations and apply findings to client projects.
* Assist clients in understanding and complying with federal, state, and local environmental requirements.
* Communicate with regulatory agencies and client representatives.
* Participate in field sampling and data collection activities.
* Collaborate with multidisciplinary project teams to deliver high\-quality environmental solutions.
* Manage multiple assignments while meeting project schedules and deadlines.
* Maintain a strong commitment to health, safety, and environmental stewardship.

What We're Looking For

* Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Geology, Biology, Chemistry, Engineering, or a related scientific discipline.
* 3\+ years of environmental compliance experience.
* Knowledge of RCRA, hazardous waste management, regulated waste, and environmental compliance regulations.
* Experience with stormwater, air quality, storage tanks, or other multimedia environmental programs.
* Strong technical writing and communication skills.
* Excellent organizational and time\-management abilities.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, and SharePoint.
* Ability to work independently and as part of a project team.
* Willingness to travel and perform field work as needed.
* Environmental auditing experience is a plus.

Why Apply?

* Diverse and challenging environmental projects.
* Opportunity to build expertise across multiple environmental media programs.
* Career growth and professional development opportunities.
* Meaningful work that helps protect the environment and support regulatory compliance.
* Collaborative team environment with experienced environmental professionals.
* Mix of office, field, and client\-facing responsibilities.

* Familiarity with federal and state environmental regulations
* Strong analytical, organizational, time management, and problem\-solving skills

jobs.description:
**THE ROLE**


Directive is a revenue\-first marketing consultancy built to serve B2B SaaS, enterprise technology, industrial, and commerce brands. We don't make things look good for its own sake. We build visual systems that hold up under the pressure of performance channels, complex professional services positioning, and a buying audience that starts with a CMO and ends with a CFO.


We are looking for an Associate Creative Director who will translate Moments that Matter into creative territories, messaging hypotheses, campaign concepts, headlines, CTAs, and copy direction that designers can execute against. The Associate Creative Director will bring senior\-level creative judgment to work that is fast\-moving, digital\-first, and tied directly to business outcomes. This person will not simply wait for polished briefs or execute one\-off design requests. They will help shape the ask, identify stronger creative angles, and translate strategic inputs into assets that feel clear, compelling, and differentiated. They will represent creative in strategic new\-business and portfolio\-sales opportunities, help build speculative and portfolio creative, and support Directive’s move toward campaign\-style case studies that can drive account growth and new revenue.

* Produced at least one example of a stronger campaign territory or messaging direction from an existing work.

* Created a first draft of the campaign creative brief template tied to Moments that Matter / Stratos.

jobs.title: Environmental Health Specialist
jobs.description:
**About FACS**


At FACS, our mission is to make environments safer and healthier for the people who live and work in them. As one of the nation's leading environmental health consulting firms, we help organizations protect their people, assets, and communities. We are built on purpose, partnership, and performance, delivering measurable impact with every client engagement.

**Our Values**


We live our mission through three core values:

* **People First:** Support our team and clients, promote professional growth, and value collaboration.
* **Integrity of the Science:** Deliver accurate, reliable results through objective, evidence\-based practices.
* **Client Relationships for Life:** Build long\-term partnerships and help clients address environmental health challenges.

**Why Join Us**

* **Impact:** Contribute meaningful work that empowers teams and drives results across the organization.
* **Culture:** Thrive in a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and mission\-driven environment where your work matters.
* **Growth:** Innovate, develop your skills, and help shape the future of how we operate and deliver on our mission.
* **Visibility:** Partner directly with leadership and cross\-functional teams to make a real difference.


Ranked "Best Places to Work" for five consecutive years, we invest in your success through training, mentorship, and support for professional certifications—so you can grow, thrive, and build a career with lasting impact.

*Curious to see what we do? Meet our team at* FACS Experts.


**About the Role:**


The Environmental Health Specialist will support public health and well\-being by conducting fieldwork and environmental assessments for a variety of environmental health and industrial hygiene projects. Under the direction of Project Managers, you will support projects involving asbestos, lead, mold and moisture, indoor environmental quality, air and exposure sampling, and other environmental health concerns.


This is a field\-based role that requires regular travel to local client sites and occasional travel outside the local area, depending on project needs. You will collect samples and field data, document site conditions, prepare accurate field notes, and communicate project updates to Project Managers.


This opportunity is ideal for someone who enjoys hands\-on work, takes pride in accuracy and professionalism, and is eager to develop technical experience in environmental health and industrial hygiene. The ideal candidate demonstrates strong attention to detail, reliability, a positive work ethic, and a willingness to learn beyond their current comfort zone.

**Responsibilities:**

* Perform assigned fieldwork and project tasks under the direction of Project Managers.
* Travel regularly to local client sites and occasionally to out\-of\-area locations based on project needs.
* Support environmental health and industrial hygiene projects involving asbestos, lead, mold and moisture, indoor environmental quality, air and exposure sampling, and other environmental health concerns.
* Review project scopes, site requirements, and field protocols to ensure a clear understanding of assigned work.
* Collect field data and samples in accordance with established procedures, project specifications, and safety requirements.
* Conduct site observations and document field conditions accurately and thoroughly.
* Prepare, organize, maintain, and transport the tools, equipment, and supplies needed for assigned fieldwork.
* Maintain detailed field notes; compile data; and summarize findings to support project reporting and analysis.
* Communicate regularly with Project Managers regarding project status, technical questions, field conditions, and next steps.
* Report progress, concerns, and deviations from project scope or established protocols promptly.
* Interact professionally and collaboratively with clients, contractors, building occupants, and other stakeholders at project sites.
* Follow all company safety procedures and use required personal protective equipment.
* Participate actively in training, mentorship, and professional\-development opportunities to build technical knowledge in environmental health and industrial hygiene.
* Support the delivery of high\-quality, timely client service while maintaining FACS’s standards for accuracy, professionalism, and integrity.

**What You Bring:**

**Required**

* High school diploma or equivalent.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills and attention to detail.
* Reliable, professional, and able to follow field protocols, safety requirements, and project instructions.
* Valid driver’s license, reliable transportation, current auto insurance, and a driving record that meets company standards.
* Ability to travel regularly to local client sites, with occasional out\-of\-area travel as needed.
* Ability to perform the essential functions of this field\-based role, with or without reasonable accommodation.
* Flexibility to work occasional evenings and weekends based on project requirements.

**Preferred**

* Associate’s or bachelor’s degree in a related field.
* Fieldwork or related experience in environmental services, construction, facilities, EHS, restoration, inspection, sampling, or technical documentation.
* Familiarity with asbestos, lead, mold and moisture, indoor environmental quality, or air and exposure sampling.

**Physical \& Work Requirements**

* Ability to perform field\-based work at client sites, including stooping, kneeling, climbing, crawling, and accessing a variety of areas to collect samples.
* Ability to lift, carry, and move equipment and instruments weighing up to 50 pounds.
* Ability to wear required personal protective equipment and complete job\-related medical surveillance and respirator fit testing, as required for assigned work and consistent with applicable law.
* Ability to work at a desk and use a computer for extended periods to complete documentation and reporting.

jobs.title: Environmental Specialist, Water
jobs.description:
**Company Overview:**

**MP Materials (NYSE: MP) is rebuilding American industrial capability for a new era of autonomy, robotics, and electrification.**


We are the only U.S. company with a fully integrated rare earth supply chain—from mining and refining to advanced metal and magnet manufacturing. Our products include both the critical materials used to make permanent magnets and the finished magnets themselves—enabling next\-generation technologies in robotics, automation, aerospace, transportation, defense, and energy systems. These materials are the foundation of physical AI—the convergence of computation, movement, and control.


We hire ambitious, mission\-driven people who want to tackle complex challenges and shape the future of strategic industries. Our culture is rooted in teamwork, resiliency, and integrity, with a deep commitment to operational excellence and national purpose. MP is rapidly evolving from a materials producer into a leading U.S. manufacturer—and our people are driving that transformation.

**Position Overview:**


Under supervision of the Environmental Manager, the Environmental Specialist serves as the technical expert for environmental compliance. The Environmental Specialist is responsible for developing strategic compliance plans and objectives to meet current, developing, and future regulatory requirements with a focus on water permitting, monitoring, reporting, and recordkeeping, while supporting continuous improvement in environmental performance across the organization. This position will ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local water quality standards and regulations.

**Position Responsibilities:**

* Oversee and actively update environmental compliance programs in assigned area of responsibility (water management).
* Maintain accurate records of water data, water system performance, and operational logs.
* Prepare and submit required reports such as Water Quality Monitoring Reports, Water Use Reports, and Site Water Reports.
* Prepare, submit, and maintain all required water permits, including California Regional Water Board, County Water Permits, and SWPPP Reports.
* Collect, analyze, and interpret water data from sources including but not limited to remote monitoring wells, freshwater wells, mine wells, and various sample data.
* Support environmental assessments for new or modified processes and projects (construction, expansion, etc.).
* Assist operations and maintenance teams with ensuring water systems (e.g., pumps, wells, pipes) operate efficiently.
* Conduct internal water compliance audits and corrective action follow\-ups.
* Develop and deliver water compliance training for employees, contractors, and supervisors.
* Track changes in water regulations and communicate potential impacts to management.
* Support company sustainability initiatives related to water balances, water recycling, and freshwater use.
* Identify opportunities to reduce environmental impact and improve compliance performance.
* Perform and document environmental, health, and safety audits.
* Develop an understanding of CalOSHA and MSHA regulations as well as MP Materials Health and Safety Practices.
* Respond to chemical spill emergencies by managing the containment, clean up, and disposal of hazardous materials.
* Keeps all levels of the facility personnel aware of environmental regulations and pending changes. Educates, clarifies, and simplifies environmental regulations, policies, and procedures into understandable and operations terms.
* Effectively maintains high level of knowledge and understanding of environmental regulations, policies, and procedures into understandable operations terms.
* Effectively maintains high level for knowledge and understanding of environmental regulations and how they apply to the facility in the areas of air, water, and solid waste management.
* Develops and provides necessary training of site personnel so that all facility employees have the knowledge and skills to comply with and enforce environmental regulations and policies. Training should emphasize Environmental over Production \- prevention, individual responsibility, and commitment.
**Basic Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in environmental or environmental related discipline is preferred.
* 4\+ years’ experience in environmental or environmental related fields.

**Desired Qualities:**

* Professional certifications not required but are a plus: CEP, QEP, and/or CES.
* CA State Water Boards D1 Operator certification is preferred; or be able to acquire certification within 6 months of hire date.
* Excellent verbal, interpersonal, and written communication skills.
* Ability to effectively train and direct others (peers, employees, contractors/vendors).
* Ability to work independently and within a team environment.
* Knowledge of industrial plant processes and equipment.
* Knowledge of industrial plant operations and maintenance requirements.
* Project management skills.
* Employee relations skills and ability to motivate others.
* Knowledge of regulatory and corrective action tracking programs.
* Knowledge of computer maintenance management tracking programs.

Candidates whose disabilities make them unable to meet the position’s requirements will still be considered qualified if they can perform the essential functions of the job with reasonable accommodation.

**Hazardous Materials** **Specialist III**
  

The County of Orange is accepting *internal* applications for **Hazardous Materials** **Specialist III.** Internal applications include a lateral transfer, reduction and reassignment. Current regular and limited\-term employees interested in a lateral transfer between agencies or departments must meet the following requirements:


* Employees may only apply for inter\-departmental transfer for positions within their same job classification and/or those comparable classifications with the same maximum salary range, for which the employee fully meets the qualifications of the lateral position.
* Employees must be in good standing in their current position, which is defined as receiving a "meets or exceeds expectations" on your last performance review.
* Employees currently serving a probationary period are eligible to apply, however, Human Resource Services must obtain Chief Human Resources Officer approval prior to a job offer.
* You also have the option of being considered for a reassignment/reduction to another class in the same or lower salary range provided you meet the minimum requirements for the class.

Email is the primary form of notification during this process. Please provide your personal email address that is accessible when out of the office and after work hours.

**Company Description**  

Founded in Denmark, Ramboll is a foundation\-owned people company. We have more than 18,000 experts working across our global operations in 35 countries with thousands of experts working across 70 offices in the Americas. Our experts are leaders in their fields, developing and delivering innovative solutions in diverse markets including Buildings, Transport, Planning \& Urban Design, Water, Environment \& Health, Energy, and Management Consulting. We invite you to contribute to a more sustainable future working in an open, collaborative, and empowering company. Combining local experience with global knowledge, we together shape the societies of tomorrow.

 **Job Description** **Preferred U.S. Locations (Hybrid):** Arlington, VA; Princeton, NJ; Boston, MA; Seattle, WA; Portland, OR; Oakland/San Francisco, CA; Irvine/Los Angeles, CA. Remote will be considered.

**Shape the Future of Environmental Health**


Are you passionate about helping clients solve complex environmental and public health challenges? Do you thrive at the intersection of science, strategy, and business development? Are you excited to work with leading experts to develop solutions that protect communities while supporting sustainable development?


Join Ramboll's Global Health Sciences team as a senior contributor and play a key leadership role in growing one of the industry's premier environmental health consulting practices.

**Your New Role**


As our new Principal, you will lead business development, client relationships, and technical delivery focused on human health risk assessment, community health, environmental health sciences, and emerging environmental challenges. You will help clients navigate complex regulatory, legal, and stakeholder environments while building trusted advisor relationships with industry, government, and legal\-sector clients.


This role combines technical excellence, strategic leadership, and commercial responsibility. You will work closely with clients and colleagues across Health Sciences, Water, Site Solutions, Sustainability, and Environment \& Health practices to deliver integrated solutions that support sound, science\-based decision making.

**Areas of Expertise**


We are interested in candidates with expertise in one or more of the following areas:

* Human health risk assessment
* Air toxics and multi\-pathway risk evaluations
* Community health and health impact assessment
* Environmental justice
* Environmental health and exposure science
* PFAS, microplastics and other emerging contaminants
* Toxicology
* Strategic risk management
* Expert services and litigation support

**Key Responsibilities**

**Business Development \& Client Leadership**

* Develop and expand client relationships across industrial, commercial, government, and legal sectors
* Identify and pursue new business opportunities aligned with practice growth objectives
* Lead proposal development, strategic pursuits, and major client accounts
* Serve as a trusted advisor to clients navigating regulatory and public health challenges
* Collaborate across Ramboll's global network to bring integrated solutions to clients

**Technical Leadership**

* Direct complex risk assessment and community health projects
* Provide technical leadership and quality assurance on key deliverables
* Communicate scientific findings to technical, regulatory, legal, and community audiences
* Support clients during stakeholder engagement, regulatory interactions, and public meetings
* Advance innovative approaches for emerging environmental and public health issues

**Thought Leadership**

* Publish technical articles and present at scientific conferences
* Participate in professional societies, industry groups, and regulatory forums
* Help shape Ramboll's market presence in environmental health sciences
* Contribute to the development of new service offerings and strategic growth initiatives

**People Leadership**

* Mentor and develop junior and mid\-level consultants
* Foster a collaborative, inclusive, and high\-performing team culture
* Support recruitment and growth of the Risk Assessment \& Community Health practice
* Help build future leaders within the Health Sciences team

**About You**


From the moment you start at Ramboll, we will support your personal and professional development so that you can continue to grow with the company. While we look forward to supporting your continued learning and development, for this role we have identified some qualifications, skills, and capabilities that will set you up for success.


Successful candidates will typically possess:

* Advanced degree (M.S., M.P.H., Ph.D., Dr.P.H., or equivalent) in Public Health, Toxicology, Environmental Health, Exposure Science, Risk Assessment, Environmental Science, or a related discipline
* 15\+ years of environmental health consulting or related experience
* Demonstrated record of successful business development and revenue generation
* Strong relationships with industry, regulatory, legal, or government clients
* Exceptional written, verbal, and presentation skills
* Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and managing complex projects
* Ability to effectively communicate technical information to diverse audiences
* Experience supporting environmental justice or community health initiatives, with litigation support or expert witness services, with PFAS, air toxics, cumulative impacts, or emerging contaminants is desired. As well as being a recognized subject matter expertise within environmental health sciences with an existing professional network capable of supporting continued practice growth.

**Why Ramboll?**


At Ramboll, you will join a global team of scientists, engineers, and consultants dedicated to creating sustainable solutions for clients and society. You will have opportunities to collaborate with leading experts across North America and internationally while helping shape the future of environmental health c

### **Job Description and Duties**


The Cap\-and\-Invest Program has a position available for a motivated Air Pollution Specialist (APS) with knowledge of forestry practices to conduct a variety of activities related to development, implementation, and analysis of the U.S Forest Compliance Offset Protocol. This work supports the California Air Resources Board’s greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reductions programs, principally the Compliance Offset Program within the Cap\-and\-Invest Program. The available APS position is in the Program Operation Section, which is situated in the Climate Change Program Evaluation Branch of the Industrial Strategies Division.  

Under direction of an Air Resources Supervisor I, the incumbent will participate as a member of high\-level technical (engineering and scientific) teams established to address technical and policy issues associated with the development of protocols and projects for the reduction of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions as part of California's Cap\-and\-Invest Program.  

The duties for this position are primarily focused on implementing the U.S Forest Compliance Offset Protocol. The incumbent will assess U.S Forest Compliance Offset Protocol projects, including forest inventory methods, and assist offset project operators with compliance and verification matters. The incumbent will develop technical and statistical tools and approaches for assessing forest carbon quantification, monitoring, and reporting applicable to the Compliance Offset Program and other forest\-related and land conservation efforts. The incumbent will take actions to address issues and questions related to the implementation of the U.S. Forest Protocol and the Cap\-and\-Invest Regulation and develop guidance to support implementation of the Compliance Offset Program. The incumbent will also be responsible for assisting with the development of updates to the U.S Forest Compliance Offset Protocol and the associated provisions in the Cap\-and\-Invest Regulation and for supporting rulemaking processes to adopt new compliance offset protocols.
The incumbent will develop a variety of reports, briefing papers, guidance documents, speeches, and presentations to communicate about the Compliance Offset Program, and will work with management to evaluate proposals and recommend creative solutions to climate change challenges. The incumbent may also be called upon to serve as a lead person for workgroups, technical meetings, and audits of verification bodies and projects, and to engage in events with industry, environmental groups, government organizations, and the public. The incumbent may assist with review of offset project types other than forest projects.  

This position requires development and assessment of GHG reduction measures; understanding and use of technical, economic, financial, and market data; consultation with stakeholders; interpretation and application of regulatory requirements; evaluation of environmental policies; and project management skills. This position requires occasional travel.  

This position may be subjected to a background check, for felonies and credit, to ensure the integrity of the carbon market program due to the position’s access to market sensitive information.
You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


This position may be eligible for hybrid in\-office work and in\-state telework. The amount of telework is at the agency's discretion and is based on the California Air Resources Board’s (CARB) current telework policy. While the CARB may support telework, some in\-person attendance is also required.


The positions at the CARB may be eligible for telework with in\-person attendance based on the operational needs of the position under Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria outlined in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of hybrid telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location at their own expense, as indicated on their duty statement.


Effective July 1, 2025, the California Department of Human Resources (CalHR) implemented the Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025\). PLP 2025 directs that each employee shall receive a 3 percent reduction in pay in exchange for 5 hours PLP 2025 leave credits, monthly. The salary range(s) included in the job advertisement do not reflect the 3 percent reduction in pay.

* Standard office environment (artificial lighting, controlled temperature, etc.).
* Daily use of a personal computer, office equipment, and/or telephone.
* Travel may be required.

Synopsis:
At the City of Melville, we're committed to creating a safe, healthy and sustainable environment for our residents. We're looking for motivated Environmental Health Officer to join our dedicated team and play a vital role in protecting public health through education, compliance and proactive environmental health initiatives.


Working within our Environmental Health team, you'll undertake a diverse range of regulatory, advisory and educational activities while partnering with residents, businesses and internal stakeholders to deliver high\-quality environmental health outcomes.


If you enjoy working collaboratively, solving complex problems and engaging with the community, we'd love to hear from you.

  

**Location:** City of Melville Civic Centre


**Salary:** $83,200\.00 to $111,296\.64 pro\-rata p.a. \+ 12% Super


**Employment Type:** Permanent, Full Time

  

**What You’ll Be Doing**


* Conducting inspections, assessments and investigations across a variety of environmental health matters
* Assessing development applications and processing environmental health applications
* Delivering proactive environmental health programs, sampling and compliance activities
* Providing professional advice to residents, businesses and internal stakeholders
* Supporting enforcement activities, including investigations and legal proceedings where required
* Mentoring the Environmental Health Assistant and contributing to continuous improvement across the team
* Assisting the Senior Environmental Health Officer in delivering efficient and effective environmental health services
  

**What We’re Looking For**


* A current ‘C’ Class Driver's Licence
* Qualifications recognised for appointment as an Environmental Health Officer in Western Australia
* Eligibility for appointment as an Authorised Person and Inspector under relevant legislation
* Demonstrated experience in environmental health inspections, investigations and compliance activities
* Sound knowledge of relevant environmental health legislation, including the Food Act 2008, Health (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1911 and Environmental Protection Act 1986
* Strong communication, negotiation and report writing skills
* The ability to manage competing priorities while delivering high\-quality customer service

Local Government experience, food safety auditing knowledge and previous mentoring experience will be highly regarded.

  

**How to Apply**


Apply online via the Apply button and provide a comprehensive resume and cover letter (no more than 2 pages) demonstrating fulfilment of essential requirements outlined in the Position Description attached.


**Closing Date: Sunday, 04 Oct 2026, 11\.59PM AWST.**


For further information about this position, please contact: **Chiat Chew, A/ Manager Health and Compliance on 08 9364 0281\.**


If you are interested in this exciting opportunity, we strongly advise you apply as soon as possible as the City reserves the right to close this advertisement before the closing date.

We are a welcoming and diverse community that enjoys a blend of retail and business precincts and an abundance of open spaces in a unique, natural landscape, along the shores of the beautiful Swan and Canning Rivers.


We are proud to be recognised as an Inclusive Employer 2024\-2025 – a prestigious award that benchmarks workplace inclusion across various diversity areas. This recognition is the only one of its kind in Australia and highlights our commitment to fostering a workplace where diversity is celebrated, and inclusion thrives. In everything we do, we focus on our EPIC values of Excellence, Participation, Integrity and Caring and we aim to achieve an inclusive, vibrant, and sustainable future.

  

**Why Belong?**


Elevate your work experience with the City of Melville’s benefits!

* Enjoy flexible working arrangements that help balance work and life
* Stay active with a free LeisureFit membership
* Save time and money with free on\-site parking

* Maximise your pay with salary packaging and novated leasing options
* Grow your career with structured professional development and study assistance programs
* Look after your wellbeing with wellness initiatives and Employee Assistance Programs
* Connect outside of work with a vibrant social club
* conditions apply


The City of Melville celebrates diversity, inclusion, and belonging. We welcome and strongly encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including but not limited to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people from culturally diverse backgrounds, and people living with disabilities.


All candidates applying for a position where the use of ‘plant and machinery’ or driving a vehicle is an inherent requirement of the role and other ‘high risk’ facilities where public safety is at risk, will be required to pass a drug and alcohol test as part of a pre\-employment medical.
